summary: OAuth hardening (Apple JWKS + Google Emergent-delegated + collision guard + rate limiting + method traceability) verified. Ran full backend pytest suite 3 consecutive times. All runs identical & green: 282 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed. All 15 new tests in test_oauth_hardening.py pass; the previously-flagged flaky tests (test_distributed_brute_force_by_ip, test_password_change_reports_revoked_count) passed cleanly in every run in the full-suite context — no cross-test bleed observed on this environment. All security guarantees exercised: Apple garbage token → 401 (JWKS), Apple <32-char token → 422 (Pydantic), Google short session_token → 422, Google empty/malformed email → 401, cross-provider collision on email/password × Google → needs_linking=True (409 path), Google-only user × Apple → needs_linking=True, same-provider re-login → no collision, /auth/login persists method='email' on session doc, /auth/google & /auth/apple both invoke check_login_rate_limit with oauth:{provider}:{ip} keys, Apple first-sign-in payload email persisted when claim.email absent. No code changes made — main agent's implementation is confirmed stable.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/auth.py:557 — Apple record_login_attempt uses `rl_key = email or f"apple:{apple_sub}"`; if `email` is empty string (Apple private-relay + no client payload) it would fall through to the apple_sub key. This is correct but worth noting: those login_attempts entries won't share the per-email 5-fails/15min counter with the same user's other providers. Not a security regression; documenting for future rate-limit audits.

routes/auth.py:207-209 — _apple_audiences() defaults include 'host.exp.Exponent' when APPLE_AUDIENCES env is unset; ensure production deploys always set APPLE_AUDIENCES explicitly so Expo Go's shared audience is not accepted in prod builds.

routes/auth.py:164 — Legacy migration path: users with no `providers[]` and no `password` are assumed 'google'. If an Apple-only legacy user existed pre-migration they would be mis-tagged as google and hit a false collision on Apple re-login. Acceptable given /auth/apple was net-new in this iteration (no such legacy users can exist).
